rationale:
Issue #287 ("`CMS.sign` ignores `additionalIntermediateCertificates` when `signingTime` is passed") states the defect as a dropped argument on the signing-time path. The minimized production patch is exactly that: one added line in Sources/X509/CryptographicMessageSyntax/CMSOperations.swift forwarding `additionalIntermediateCertificates:` into `self.signWithSigningTime(...)`. The trigger test `testSigningWithSigningTimeSignedAttrAndIntermediates` calls the pre-existing public `CMS.sign` overload with both `additionalIntermediateCertificates:` and `signingTime:` and then verifies the chain against a root-only trust store, so it fails on the buggy revision because the intermediate is absent from the produced CMS blob, not because of any API introduced by the fix; the buggy revision compiled and ran the test (trigger.buggy_differential reproduced this selector while the second declared selector `testSigningWithSigningTimeSignedAttrAndSHA512` passed), confirming no new production API dependency. The patch touches a single production file with one hunk and no formatting, refactor, doc, or config changes; the test addition is isolated in patches/trigger-tests.patch. Strict evidence passes on both the original and post-minimization matrices (build.both_versions, trigger.deterministic with 3 repetitions, trigger.fixed_clean, full_suite.fixed_all_green, full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers) with no failed checks. active_same_project_root_causes is empty and apple/swift-certificates#287 is in allowed_root_cause_ids, so the root cause is not a duplicate of any active registry entry.

Issue #287 ("`CMS.sign` ignores `additionalIntermediateCertificates` when `signingTime` is passed") names exactly the omission the production fix repairs: the single added line in Sources/X509/CryptographicMessageSyntax/CMSOperations.swift forwards `additionalIntermediateCertificates:` to `self.signWithSigningTime(...)` in the signingTime branch of `CMS.sign`. Traceability is fix_commit -> merged PR #289 (single commit, merge_commit_sha equals fixed_revision 7d5f612) -> issue 287, with verified_fix_issue_numbers=[287]. The minimized patch is the whole production change: 1 original hunk, 1 retained, 0 removed, one added argument line, no signature change, no formatting/docs/config/test content. Because only a call-site argument is added and the callee signature is untouched, the fix introduces no new production API, so the trigger cannot depend on one: testSigningWithSigningTimeSignedAttrAndIntermediates calls the pre-existing `CMS.sign(_:signatureAlgorithm:additionalIntermediateCertificates:certificate:privateKey:signingTime:)` overload with an intermediate plus leaf2Cert/leaf2Key and then verifies against a store holding only rootCert, which fails on the buggy revision precisely because the intermediate never reaches the SignedData and the chain cannot be built. The trigger is the unaltered upstream test hunk from the fixing commit, not curator-written. Strict evidence passes identically pre- and post-minimization: build.both_versions, trigger.buggy_differential (reproduced selector = testSigningWithSigningTimeSignedAttrAndIntermediates), trigger.fixed_clean, trigger.deterministic (3 outcome groups over 3 repetitions, 38 matrix runs), full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers, and full_suite.fixed_all_green, with no failed_checks. active_same_same_project_root_causes is empty, so no registry duplicate exists, and apple/swift-certificates#287 is the sole allowed_root_cause_id.

The trigger asserts end-to-end chain validation rather than directly inspecting the CMS certificate set, so it could in principle be sensitive to unrelated verification-policy regressions; the fixed-revision green suite and deterministic 3x differential mitigate but do not eliminate this.

Evidence grade is portable_release_evidence with full-suite repetitions of 1, so flakiness at full-suite scope is less thoroughly sampled than the 3x isolated trigger runs.
